label: GO
call: Run a capped 90-day paid Site Decision Brief service for Kigali-based real-estate developers. Use manual delivery to prove demand, margins and a repeatable workflow, then productise only what customers repeatedly pay for.

why.point: There is no verified evidence of paid demand or repeatable unit economics. Five paying customers matter more than another round of feature development.
The first offer should solve one expensive developer decision, with payment collected before research begins.
why.framework: One Product, One Avatar, One Channel

why.point: Public land data is an input, not the moat. The asset must be trusted, sourced, current and reusable.

minority.quote: C can turn Taiseel into a well-paid research desk with no leverage.
minority.would_have_to_be_true: The pilot fails to produce permissioned reusable data or a workflow that customers want repeatedly; in that case a narrow software-first product may be better.

next_steps.action: Define the paid Site Decision Brief, data-source register, exclusions and deposit terms.
Complete 20 qualified developer conversations and secure paid pilot work.
Review five paid reports, repeat demand, contribution margin and the productisation decision.

kill_criteria: Stop or reshape if fewer than three of 20 qualified buyers pay, reports do not change a real decision, direct delivery cost stays above 70% of fees after five reports, or reliable lawful data cannot be secured.
conditions: At least five paid assessments within 90 days.
At least two repeat orders, retainer requests or referrals.
By the fifth report, target direct delivery costs below 50% of collected fees.
All material claims show source, date and confidence; no legal title or valuation guarantees.
No new hires, borrowing, personal guarantees or speculative development commitments during the test.

fights.story: Seven seats favoured a paid service test; Naval maintained a product-first dissent. Bezos, Gary V and Wickman moved from B to C after treating the pilot as a reversible learning step.

fights.crux: What is the moat if land data is public?
fights.story: The room agreed that public data and a map interface alone are not defensible. The possible moat is trusted provenance, updated history, interpretation and a repeatable workflow.
The development/JV proposition and the software/intelligence product require separate economics, contracts and capital decisions.

amendments.amendment: Keep the 90-day limit and productisation gate.
amendments.reason: Prevents an indefinite service business and keeps the test reversible.

amendments.amendment: Collect a deposit before starting and calculate gross profit after delivery hours.
amendments.reason: Separates real buying behaviour from polite interest.

amendments.amendment: Publish one sourced insight weekly without exposing client information.
amendments.reason: Creates distribution among the target audience while protecting data integrity.

amendments.amendment: Track founder hours and prohibit premature hiring.
amendments.reason: Makes founder capacity and labour economics visible.

amendments.amendment: One owner and one weekly delivery scorecard.
amendments.reason: Makes quality and execution accountable without adding bureaucracy.

amendments.amendment: No debt, guarantees, speculative land purchases or blended JV cash.
amendments.reason: Caps downside and separates capital-intensive activity from the pilot.

amendments.amendment: Require permissioned reusable data and an explicit productisation milestone.
amendments.reason: Protects the goal of building an owned software and data asset, even though Naval still dissents on the sequencing.

cheapest_test: Offer ten Kigali developers a paid assessment for one live parcel decision. Collect a deposit before doing the research.
revisit: 2027-02-19, with paid customers, repeat/referral count, fees, delivery hours and costs, report corrections, turnaround, lead source and cash/runway.
override_note: No seat ended at likely ruin risk. C is a reversible 90-day test with no new debt, guarantees, land commitments or fixed-cost expansion.
